proposal.diagnosis: Across several failures, the agent stopped on an unverified or already-disproven state because completion was accepted from a plain assistant message instead of being tied to a real successful check in tool history. The traces show this concretely. In regex-log, it ran `python3 /app/test_regex.py` twice and both times got `[]`, then still ended after 6 model calls with `stop_reason: agent_declared_complete`. In configure-git-webserver, it saw `systemctl: command not found` with exit 127 and `nginx -s reload` fail with `invalid PID number`, never ran a self-check like `curl`, and still ended after 19 model calls; the verifier later reported HTTP 301. In fix-code-vulnerability, pytest reported `IndentationError` in `/app/bottle.py`, the agent edited the file with `sed -i`, and then stopped after 73 model calls without rerunning pytest. I cannot prove every miss has the same root cause, and build-cython-ext likely also needed better task understanding, but the repeated evidence-supported pattern is premature completion without a validated final check.
proposal.rationale: A focused fix is to change completion from an unchecked plain-text exit into an explicit `finish` tool call that must cite a real successful bash command from the conversation as its final verification. The dispatcher validates that the cited command actually ran, succeeded, and occurred after the latest write-like change, with no later writes or failed commands. This directly targets the observed failure pattern while avoiding the brittle command-name whitelist that previously rejected valid ad hoc checks such as silent `test -f ...` or custom `python -c 'assert ...'` commands. The assistant can use any verification command it wants; the runtime only checks recency and success against actual history. Rejections come back as concise tool results, so repeated completion interventions stay bounded. This will not catch every semantic mistake if the agent verifies the wrong property, so there is some uncertainty, but it should prevent the specific recurring behavior of declaring success after failed, stale, or missing verification.

limitations: Two development repetitions and three held-out tasks are too small to establish a reliable general gain.
The candidate received an operator review and revision before benchmarking; ordinary API jobs remain automatic.
Both agents use gpt-4.1-mini. Only the proposal optimizer changed to pinned GPT-5.4 with medium reasoning.
No task outcomes were dropped; no candidate edits followed the frozen evaluation plan.
Token usage is provider-reported, not a billing estimate. Failed proposal usage is unavailable.
Command success, heuristic write detection and approximate command matching do not prove correct task verification.
The first candidate damaged its own filesystem on configure-git-webserver. Its missing verifier reward is retained and explicitly assessed as a zero-score agent failure; the task was not retried.
